title: fenwick marsh q3 2026 workload tracker
instruction:
You are the project management specialist coordinating Fenwick Marsh Environmental’s Q3 2026 permitting portfolio for Rhiannon Setterfield. Rhiannon has to confirm client leads with Saltcombe Provisions and Westmere Logistics by Friday, 26 June 2026, and she needs a staffed quarter rather than another provisional capacity list. The attached `q3_permitting_workload.xlsx` contains the nine deliverables, activity effort, dependencies, delivery windows, consultant availability, competence and approval records, development commitments, and the England permitting control note that applies as at 15 May 2026. It also carries the reporting terms used by the portfolio team. Treat the listed weekly capacity as the time remaining after other committed work; we are not adding people or moving work outside the quarter. Prepare `q3_workload_tracker.xlsx` and write it into the top level of the working directory using exactly that filename. The workbook needs to let Rhiannon and a compliance reviewer establish the following without reconstructing your reasoning: (1) give every deliverable one accountable owner, identify any supporting consultant and approved submission signatory where applicable, and show the allocation of each person’s available time by deliverable and week; (2) schedule every listed activity within the Q3 workweeks, respecting its delivery window, duration, dependencies, competence requirements, unavailable periods, and any activities that cannot share a week, with the final portfolio complete by Friday, 25 September 2026; (3) apply the client-facing submission and independent-review controls in the source, including the limits on who may sign, but do not treat signatory status as a blanket rule for who can own the underlying work; (4) deal explicitly with Casimir Oyelowo’s supervised-submission approval window while keeping the resulting plan feasible and properly supervised; (5) include a consultant summary showing weekly planned hours, available hours, utilisation percentage, remaining capacity or overload, and quarter totals, plus a deliverable summary that reconciles to the detailed schedule; (6) give a concise, person-specific reason for each accountable-owner choice, grounded in the competence, relevant experience, availability, client continuity, or documented development evidence in the source, and briefly record why another plausible candidate was not selected where the choice could reasonably be questioned; and (7) include a short assumptions and decision log for any conservative interpretation you make, without inventing approvals, competencies, extra capacity, or changes to the England control note. Keep calculations live rather than typing summary totals, make the detailed schedule filterable, and provide visible warnings for overloads, unmet dependencies, missing signatory coverage, work outside its allowed window, or the prohibited same-week combinations. The final workbook should contain a clear assignment register, an activity-level weekly schedule, consultant and deliverable summaries, and the assumptions and decision record. It will be read on screen and exported for the quarterly oversight pack, so labels, dates, percentages, legends, and warning states must remain legible and unambiguous without relying on hidden cells or undocumented colour meanings.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/q3_permitting_workload.xlsx` — Provides the nine Q3 permitting deliverables, activity effort and dependencies, delivery windows, consultant capacities and availability, competence and signatory records, development commitments, mutually exclusive activity rules, the applicable England control note as at 15 May 2026, and Fenwick Marsh reporting terminology.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `q3_workload_tracker.xlsx` — A regulator-ready Q3 resource and workload distribution tracker covering accountable ownership, activity scheduling, weekly allocations, capacity, submission controls, selection rationale, and decision assumptions. (Must be created at the top level of the working directory using exactly q3_workload_tracker.xlsx.; Must cover all nine supplied deliverables and all supplied activities through the quarter ending 25 September 2026.; Must include an assignment register, an activity-level weekly schedule, consultant and deliverable summaries, and an assumptions and decision record.; Summary calculations and warning states must remain live and auditable in the workbook.; Detailed records must be filterable, and all visible content must remain legible when reviewed on screen or exported.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

spec.professional_context: Fenwick Marsh Environmental is allocating a constrained quarterly permitting portfolio across six consultants before client leads are confirmed. The workbook will support Rhiannon Setterfield’s bounded staffing decision and subsequent compliance oversight.
difficulty_sources: Reconciling activity dependencies, delivery windows, competence, leave, and week-specific capacity across a thirteen-week quarter.
Scheduling two long major-permit chains around scarce discipline-specific signatories and same-week exclusion rules.
Meeting Casimir Oyelowo’s bounded supervised-submission development commitment without treating signatory status as an ownership requirement.
Producing live, reconciling spreadsheet summaries and conflict warnings alongside defensible person-specific staffing rationales.

instance.planning_horizon: Thirteen Monday-to-Friday workweeks from 29 June through 25 September 2026.

item_pool_size.activities: Use compact activity chains: six activities for each major permit and two to four for each remaining deliverable.

Marisol Reinholt.competence_profile: Approved client-facing signatory for water, wetlands, and integrated permit submissions; strong Saltcombe continuity.

Ravi Moravec.competence_profile: Approved client-facing signatory for air, waste, and logistics-depot submissions; strong Westmere continuity.

Chidi Jankowski.competence_profile: Ecology, drainage, water evidence, and independent technical review; not an approved submission signatory.

Arjun Redmayne.competence_profile: Air modelling, emissions inventories, noise, and quantitative analysis; not an approved submission signatory.

Lorcan Dimitrov.competence_profile: Waste operations, site audits, permit registers, and operational controls; not an approved submission signatory.

Casimir Oyelowo.competence_profile: Water and wetlands permitting, drafting, and client preparation; not yet an approved signatory.
Casimir Oyelowo.development_commitment: Must own and complete one qualifying supervised major submission by the end of W08. Only the water or wetlands major permit is competence-eligible for him.

content_requirements: Include nine synthetic deliverables split between Saltcombe Provisions and Westmere Logistics, with stable deliverable IDs.
Designate one Saltcombe water or wetlands variation and one Westmere air variation as the two major permits.

Give each activity a stable ID, deliverable link, required effort, required competence tags, earliest week, latest week, duration, split or continuity status, predecessor links, and any required role such as drafter, independent reviewer, supervisor, or signatory.
Provide week-specific net capacity and unavailability for all six consultants, plus competence, client continuity, signatory scope, and relevant development evidence.

Include an England permitting control note effective 15 May 2026 stating which activities require client-facing sign-off, discipline-appropriate approval, independent review, and supervised-submission evidence.

Carry the local meanings of accountable owner, support allocation, planned hours, available hours, utilisation, remaining capacity, major submission, qualifying supervised submission, and independent review.
Include reporting vocabulary sufficient for the solver to identify the required assignment, schedule, summary, warning, rationale, and assumptions fields without guessing local codes.

deliverable_structure.D1: Saltcombe major water or wetlands permit variation. Six-stage chain: scope, site evidence, technical assessment, draft, independent assurance, client submission. Earliest W02, completion no later than W08. This is the only qualifying major permit matching Casimir Oyelowo's competence, so the development rule makes him accountable owner in every feasible solution. Marisol Reinholt is the discipline-appropriate supervisor and signatory.
deliverable_structure.D2: Westmere major air permit variation. Six-stage chain: scope, site test, model, draft, independent assurance, client submission. Earliest W03, completion no later than W11. Ravi Moravec is the discipline-appropriate signatory; Arjun Redmayne is a strong non-signatory owner or technical-lead candidate.
deliverable_structure.D3_to_D9: Use seven smaller but material deliverables covering ecology screening, waste controls, noise, drainage, solvent inventory, trade-effluent pre-application, and a quarterly permit register. Give each a two-to-four-stage chain, a bounded window, competence requirements, and enough effort to make weekly capacity consequential.

hard_constraints: Each deliverable has exactly one accountable owner from the six-person roster.
Each activity is scheduled exactly once and receives its full required effort; non-splittable work remains intact and continuity-designated work occupies consecutive weeks.
All activity competence tags must be held by the assigned person.
For every person-week, activity, reviewer, supervision, and signatory hours together must not exceed the source net capacity; no effort may be assigned during zero-capacity leave.
Every dependency edge requires predecessor completion before successor start.
Every activity stays within its earliest-start and latest-finish window, and all work finishes by 25 September 2026.
Only Marisol Reinholt and Ravi Moravec may sign client-facing submissions, and only within their recorded discipline scopes.
Major permits require an approved discipline-appropriate signatory and an independent reviewer different from the drafter.
Casimir Oyelowo must own D1 and complete its supervised client-facing submission by the end of W08 under Marisol Reinholt; supporting someone else's submission does not count.
The D1 and D2 major submission activities may not occur in the same workweek.

Create at least two additional source-visible exclusion pairs tied to shared site access: the D1 site-evidence activity versus a Saltcombe ecology walkover, and the D2 site-test activity versus a Westmere waste audit. Each pair must occupy different workweeks regardless of assignee.
The accountable owner performs the source-designated ownership milestones, while specialist analysis, independent review, and signatory work may be allocated to eligible support personnel.
Owner and support allocations equal the underlying scheduled hours; all person, deliverable, week, and quarter summaries reconcile.

contention_and_tightness.target_tightness: Approximately 0.70, with a feasible solution but little slack on both major-permit chains.
contention_and_tightness.critical_path: D1 spans W02-W08 with six ordered stages and no more than one week of total slack; D2 spans W03-W11 with six ordered stages and limited slack. Submission separation and site-access exclusions should remove the obvious earliest-start placement.
contention_and_tightness.scarce_resources: Only Marisol Reinholt and Ravi Moravec can sign. Their discipline scopes prevent simple interchangeability, and their reduced-capacity or leave weeks must affect feasible placement.
contention_and_tightness.capacity_pressure: Tune activity effort so at least four consultant-weeks in a reference solution are at or above 90% utilisation and moving either major submission to the most obvious alternate week causes a capacity, leave, or exclusion conflict.
contention_and_tightness.anti_greedy_requirement: An earliest-start assignment with each deliverable given to the most senior eligible consultant must fail at least the Casimir development requirement and one weekly capacity or same-week exclusion constraint.

soft_preferences.preference: Use recorded client continuity where it does not defeat competence, capacity, independence, or the Casimir development commitment.
Avoid unnecessary fragmentation of support work across consultants.
Keep utilisation balanced enough that avoidable overload warnings are not created.

intended_verdict.gold_form: Constraint checker plus at least one solver-generated feasible workbook population.
intended_verdict.validation: Run a CP-SAT or mixed-integer solver over owner, activity-week, assignee, reviewer, supervisor, and signatory variables. Confirm every hard constraint is satisfiable, record binding constraints and utilisation, then verify that the reference workbook population satisfies every rubric predicate and workbook-behaviour test.

reference_files.purpose: Provides the nine Q3 permitting deliverables, activity effort and dependencies, delivery windows, consultant capacities and availability, competence and signatory records, development commitments, mutually exclusive activity rules, the applicable England control note as at 15 May 2026, and Fenwick Marsh reporting terminology.
reference_files.discovery: Review the full workbook, including the operational records, policy material, and reporting conventions, before assigning owners or scheduling activities.

deliverables.description: A regulator-ready Q3 resource and workload distribution tracker covering accountable ownership, activity scheduling, weekly allocations, capacity, submission controls, selection rationale, and decision assumptions.
constraints: Must be created at the top level of the working directory using exactly q3_workload_tracker.xlsx.
Must cover all nine supplied deliverables and all supplied activities through the quarter ending 25 September 2026.
Must include an assignment register, an activity-level weekly schedule, consultant and deliverable summaries, and an assumptions and decision record.
Summary calculations and warning states must remain live and auditable in the workbook.
Detailed records must be filterable, and all visible content must remain legible when reviewed on screen or exported.
